verified_by_source_review: Positive even Request dimensions and exact input dimensions precede allocation. long pixel/address calculations and Java array-size limits protect the later int indexing; 3 bytes per full-resolution pixel is the total short-array payload.

Plane buffers are readonly cursor snapshots. Explicit two-byte little-endian assembly does not depend on ByteBuffer byte order; nonzero low six bits are rejected; all 10-bit codes 0..1023 including LIMITED headroom are copied without clipping.
Three logical Y/Cb/Cr planes are handled independently with Y stride 2 and Cb/Cr stride 4; no additional Cr byte offset is applied. Only full-frame crop is supported.

Core compares exact owner/session/reader/request/callback/shot/camera/physical identities before and after copying; source and submitted result are checked, actual request must match, timestamps must match exactly under SENSOR_START_OF_EXPOSURE.

For physical output, adapter selects the named physical result before reading SENSOR_TIMESTAMP/exposure/sensitivity. Logical active physical ID is recorded separately rather than used as an implicit physical binding.
Core copies into fresh private short arrays and exposes readonly ShortBuffer views; HdrFrame has no Image or plane-buffer aliases.

copyBorrowed has no close call. copyAndClose has one try-with-resources ownership boundary and does not manually close a second time. Host tests cover success/rejection close counts and suppression of a throwing close during rejection.

README explicitly states inactive-source scope, HLG-only/full-frame subset, caller-provided provenance, serialized lifecycle and commit obligation, payload-only memory cap, no silent fallback, and no phone validation.
Adapter rejects extra/unrecognized dataspace bits rather than silently discarding bits through standard/transfer/range masks; the added extra-bit case rejects COLOR in the host suite.
limitations: No claim about actual SM-S948Q P010/HLG10 frame delivery, desired stream combinations, native resolution, camera ISP precision or scene dynamic range.

Source provenance tokens and timestamp convention must be established by the future session/callback owner. Android Image offers no public original reader/request identity; the adapter cannot independently prove these external claims.

Concurrent Image close/memory mutation and session/use races are excluded by the documented exclusive/serialized caller contract. Before/after snapshots alone cannot make arbitrary concurrent native buffer access safe.
maxAllocationBytes caps sample-array payload only, not VM headers, source Image, other live frames or future processing memory; Java allocation failure remains an error.
